$comment: Answers for a headless scaffold run:
This is what makes the template usable without a terminal you can type
into — from a phone, a web session, or CI. Copy this file, edit it, run it.
Each remote step takes one of three answers, and the third is the point:
true    — do it now (needs the CLI, logged in)
false   — I do not want this
"later" — I want it, but this environment cannot do it: the run prints
the exact command in its closing to-do list instead.
Absent means false, so a forgotten key never triggers something remote.
No secrets belong in this file. Tokens go in .env.local, which is gitignored.
name: my-site
$comment_modules: Optional modules to install, by id. Omit or leave empty for none.
Run `node scripts/setup.mjs --modules-only` later to add one you skipped.
$comment_github: push:   push the first commit to an origin that already exists (the flow
you get from 'Use this template', which sets origin for you).
create: create a new PRIVATE repo and push. Needs the gh CLI, which a
cloud/web session does not have — an assistant can do this over
the GitHub API instead, then set origin and push.
$comment_sanity: mode: "create" makes a new Sanity project, "existing" uses the projectId
below, "later" defers with the command printed at the end, false skips.
"create" and a login check need the sanity CLI, which a cloud/web session
does not have — but "existing" plus a projectId needs NO CLI at all, so a
phone session that already knows the project id can finish this step.
organization is only needed when the account belongs to more than one; the
run fails with a message naming the flag if so.
token: true mints a viewer-role read token and writes it to .env.local
(never here). Only needed for drafts and live preview.
cors: a new Sanity project allows no browser origins at all, so /studio
cannot log in and SanityLive cannot connect until http://localhost:3000
and the production URL are allowed WITH credentials. "create" does this
for the project it just made unless you set cors to false. Linking an
existing project only touches its CORS policy when cors is true — someone
else's allow-list may be deliberate. Needs the sanity CLI, so "later"
defers it with the exact commands.
$comment_vercel: Needs the vercel CLI, logged in. Same story as Sanity.
link runs `vercel link --yes`, which takes the detected Next.js build
settings rather than asking — see docs/deploy.md for what those are — then
pushes every non-empty value from .env.local to the project. A localhost
NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL is pushed to development only.
scope is the team slug, when the project does not belong to your personal
account. Leave it out for personal.
